title: FlashInfer: Efficient and Customizable Attention Engine for LLM Inference Serving
technique: block-sparse/composable KV formats, JIT-customizable attention templates, load-balanced CUDAGraph-compatible scheduler

optimized_metrics.evidence: In FlashInfer, the load-balanced scheduling algorithm aims to minimize SM idle time by distributing the workload evenly across all SMs.

headline_claim.text: FlashInfer achieve 29-69% inter-token-latency reduction compared to compiler backends for LLM serving benchmark, 28-30% latency reduction for long-context inference, and 13-17% speedup for LLM serving with parallel generation.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We measure the TTFT(time-to-first-token) and ITL(inter-token-latency) under latency-sensitive online serving settings, the request rate is adjusted to maintain P99 TTFT below 200ms.
metric_definitions.notes: Neither TTFT nor ITL is formally defined; queueing inclusion unstated.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Figure 7. Medium Inter-Token-Latency (ITL) and medium Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) of SGLang integrated with FlashInfer
metric_definitions.notes: 'Medium' is presumably median (P50). Appendix G expands ITL as 'Inference Time Latency' (inconsistent).

slo_spec: No SLO attainment; single constraint P99 TTFT < 200 ms used to pick the request rate
load_regime: request-rate sweep tuned to P99 TTFT<200ms (online); fixed rate 16 for vLLM test
hardware: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 (also A100, Ada 6000 microbenchmarks)
workloads: ShareGPT; synthetic Variable U(512,2048); U(4096,16384) in/256 out
